description: Busco formar un equipo comprometido, con buena comunicación y ganas de aprender. Me gustaría colaborar con personas que tengan conocimientos en ciencia de datos, IA/ML, astronomía, diseño UI/UX o análisis científico para desarrollar una solución creativa y funcional.
summary:
We developed "Apollo 11: A Giant Leap," an interactive web-based video game that recreates the Apollo 11 mission that took humans to the Moon in 1969. The player goes through the mission in stages and takes control of key moments, such as the launch and the moon landing. The game can be played from any browser, without having to install anything.

With this project, we want to bring a historical event closer to people, especially the youth, in a more practical and entertaining way than reading about it in a book. Playing helps you understand how difficult each step of the mission was and the hard work of the people who made it possible.

It is important because it combines history, science, and technology into an experience that sparks curiosity about space exploration.
details:
What it does and how it works. It is a 3D web game that recreates the Apollo 11 mission. The player goes through the stages of the mission: preparation, launch, journey to the Moon, lunar descent, surface walk (planting the flag, collecting scientific samples, and taking photos), and a final report. It can be played solo, accompanied by an assistant named Pancho, or in a two-player mode. In the two-player mode, one player joins the room using a code or a QR code from another device. The game is available in Spanish and English and works directly in the browser, without having to install anything.

Expected benefits and impact. It helps people learn about the mission in a practical, hands-on way. Each phase demonstrates why it was difficult, such as controlling the descent with limited fuel. It is designed for students and the general public interested in space. The cooperative mode fosters teamwork, just like in the real mission.

Tools used. JavaScript, Three.js for 3D graphics, Vite for building, Howler for audio, and a Node.js server with WebSockets for the two-player rooms and QR codes. We used 3D models of the spacesuit and lunar equipment. We also wrote automated tests for the game's physics and assets, and we published the game on our own server.

Creativity. It combines simulation, history, and cooperation between two people. The descent physics testing helps it feel like a real challenge without being overly complicated.

Factors considered. Historical accuracy, ease of play for anyone, accessibility from any device with a web browser, bilingual support (two languages), and smooth performance on standard internet connections.
